# Porting plan for iOS app to Android (2026-02-25 12:13Z)

_**User**_

I want to create / update the porting plan. For this I have imported the already existing and fully features iOS App into the folder. It can be found here: @ios-app-for-reference-during-porting/miataru

Do a full analysis of the ios app and go ahead with the plan

Development Guide - miataru Android App\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Quick Start for Developers\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Prerequisites\\\\\\\\n- Android Studio Koala+ (Electric Eel or newer recommended)\\\\\\\\n- Android SDK Platform 35 (Android 15) and build tools installed\\\\\\\\n- JDK 17\\\\\\\\n- An Android 8.0+ device or emulator (minSdk 24; targetSdk 35)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Setup\\\\\\\\n1. Clone the repository\\\\\\\\n2. Open the project root in Android Studio\\\\\\\\n3. Ensure the Android SDK 35 is installed and select the matching JDK 17\\\\\\\\n4. Sync Gradle and build the &#96;app&#96; module\\\\\\\\n5. Create and run an Android 15 emulator or use a physical device\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Project Structure Deep Dive\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Core Architecture\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\napp/\\\\\\\\n├── src/main/\\\\\\\\n│   ├── java/com/miataru/\\\\\\\\n│   │   ├── ui/                    # Compose UI (screens, components)\\\\\\\\n│   │   ├── location/              # FusedLocation + Foreground Service\\\\\\\\n│   │   ├── settings/              # DataStore + settings models\\\\\\\\n│   │   ├── data/                  # Room/DataStore, repositories, entities\\\\\\\\n│   │   ├── network/               # Miataru API client (Retrofit/Ktor)\\\\\\\\n│   │   ├── di/                    # Hilt modules\\\\\\\\n│   │   └── util/                  # Utilities\\\\\\\\n│   └── res/                       # Resources &amp; localization\\\\\\\\n└── build.gradle.kts               # Module Gradle config\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Key Dependencies\\\\\\\\n- Jetpack Compose (Material 3, Navigation, Lifecycle)\\\\\\\\n- Google Play Services Location (FusedLocationProvider)\\\\\\\\n- Hilt for dependency injection\\\\\\\\n- Retrofit or Ktor + Kotlinx Serialization for API client\\\\\\\\n- Room or DataStore for persistence\\\\\\\\n- ML Kit or ZXing for QR scanning and ZXing for QR generation\\\\\\\\n- WorkManager for background tasks\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Development Workflow\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Code Organization\\\\\\\\n- Composables should be stateless when possible; hoist state to ViewModels\\\\\\\\n- ViewModels expose immutable UI state via &#96;StateFlow&#96;/&#96;UiState&#96;\\\\\\\\n- Repositories coordinate network and local storage\\\\\\\\n- Keep platform concerns (permissions, services) outside composables\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Testing Strategy\\\\\\\\n- Unit tests for repositories/managers with JUnit and coroutines-test\\\\\\\\n- UI tests with Compose UI testing\\\\\\\\n- Instrumentation tests for location service and QR scanning\\\\\\\\n- Test on multiple device sizes and Android versions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Debugging Tips\\\\\\\\n- Use emulator location tools (route playback) for testing\\\\\\\\n- Monitor battery and background restrictions (Settings &gt; Battery)\\\\\\\\n- Trace foreground service notifications and WorkManager jobs\\\\\\\\n- Inspect network with Android Studio Network Inspector\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Common Development Tasks\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Adding New Features\\\\\\\\n1. Create a screen in &#96;ui/feature/&#96; and a &#96;FeatureViewModel&#96;\\\\\\\\n2. Add repository/manager if business logic is needed\\\\\\\\n3. Update DataStore/Room schemas if required\\\\\\\\n4. Add localized strings in &#96;res/values/strings.xml&#96;\\\\\\\\n5. Add navigation route and preview\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Location Permission Handling\\\\\\\\n- Check &#96;ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION&#96;/&#96;ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION&#96; prior to use\\\\\\\\n- Request &#96;ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION&#96; only when necessary with clear rationale\\\\\\\\n- Show UI rationale and handle permanently denied states\\\\\\\\n- Respect user choices and provide in-app toggles\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Settings \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"2.0\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\ninfo:\\\\\\\\n version: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"1.1.0\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n title: Miataru\\\\\\\\n description: |\\\\\\\\n   The Miataru API is very simple and straight forward. Generally you're posting (HTTP POST) a JSON formatted request to a service method locations and you get back a JSON formatted answer. Please take into consideration that this has the request-for-comment status and that it can change while there's work done on client and server applications. Versioning therefore is done by prepending the version number - /v1/ for version 1 - to the method call.\\\\\\\\n   \\\\\\\\n   API Version 1.1 introduces security and privacy enhancements:\\\\\\\\n   - RequestMiataruDeviceID (Mandatory) - Required for all GetLocation and GetLocationHistory requests\\\\\\\\n   - RequestMiataruDeviceKey (Optional) - Optional requester key for strict GetLocation/GetLocationHistory requester validation\\\\\\\\n   - DeviceKey authentication for write operations and visitor history access\\\\\\\\n   - Device slogan API with mandatory DeviceKey authentication\\\\\\\\n   - Allowed devices list for granular access control to location data\\\\\\\\n   - strictDeviceKeyCheck (Default: true) - Enforces requester DeviceKey validation in GetLocation/GetLocationHistory when requester key is configured\\\\\\\\n   - Broad backward compatibility with API 1.0 clients (GetLocation/GetLocationHistory require RequestMiataruDeviceID)\\\\\\\\n contact:\\\\\\\\n  name: Miataru Team\\\\\\\\n  email: info@miataru.com\\\\\\\\n  url: http://miataru.com\\\\\\\\n license:\\\\\\\\n  name: Public Domain\\\\\\\\n  url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miataru/miataru-protocol-specification/master/LICENSE\\\\\\\\n# during dev, should point to your local machine\\\\\\\\nhost: service.miataru.com\\\\\\\\nbasePath: /v1\\\\\\\\nschemes:\\\\\\\\n # tip: remove http to make production-grade\\\\\\\\n - http\\\\\\\\n - https\\\\\\\\nconsumes:\\\\\\\\n - application/json\\\\\\\\nproduces:\\\\\\\\n - application/json\\\\\\\\npaths:\\\\\\\\n /UpdateLocation:\\\\\\\\n  post:\\\\\\\\n   tags:\\\\\\\\n   - updateLocation\\\\\\\\n   description: |\\\\\\\\n     This method is used to update the location of a device. The device does not need to be known already to the Miataru server but it rather creates a unique identifier for itself in the client application. This unique identifier, or device ID is then used to address this particular device.\\\\\\\\n     \\\\\\\\n     API 1.1: If a DeviceKey has been set for a device (via /setDeviceKey), the DeviceKey parameter must be provided in each MiataruLocation element and must match the stored key. If the keys do not match, a 403 Forbidden error is returned.\\\\\\\\n   operationId: updateLocation\\\\\\\\n   produces:\\\\\\\\n   - application/json\\\\\\\\n   parameters:\\\\\\\\n   - name: body\\\\\\\\n     in: body\\\\\\\\n     description: the body of this UpdateLocation POST request contains the JSON formatted parameters.\\\\\\\\n     required: true\\\\\\\\n     schema:\\\\\\\\n      $ref: '#/definitions/MiataruUpdateLocationRequest'\\\\\\\\n   responses:\\\\\\\\n    200:\\\\\\\\n     description: successful request\\\\\\\\n     schema:\\\\\\\\n      $ref: '#/definitions/ACK'\\\\\\\\n    403:\\\\\\\\n     description: Forbidden - DeviceKey mismatch or missing when required\\\\\\\\n     schema:\\\\\\\\n      $ref: '#/definitions/Error'\\\\\\\\n /GetLocation:\\\\\\\\n  post:\\\\\\\\n   tags:\\\\\\\\n   - getLocation\\\\\\\\n   description: |\\\\\\\\n     To retrieve a specific devices latest known location the /GetLocation method is used.\\\\\\\\n     \\\\\\\\n     API 1.1 BREAKING CHANGE: RequestMiataruDeviceID is now mandatory. Requests without RequestMiataruDeviceID will return 400 Bad Request.\\\\\\\\n     \\\\\\\\n     RequestMiataruDeviceID should be the ID of the device the request is sent from (or an identifier like an URL). This is used for access control and visitor history tracking.\\\\\\\\n     \\\\\\\\n     API 1.1: If strictDeviceKeyCheck is enabled (default), and the requesting device (RequestMiataruDeviceID) has a configured DeviceKey, MiataruConfig.RequestMiataruDeviceKey must match or the server returns 403 Forbidden.\\\\\\\\n     \\\\\\\\n     API 1.1: If an allowed devices list has been set for a device (via /setAllowedDeviceList), only devices with hasCurrentLocationAccess permission will receive location data. Devices without permission will receive the location as if the device doesn't exist. Public API (classes, interfaces, main methods)\\\\n\\\\n**Entry point**\\\\n\\\\n- **&#96;MiataruAndroidClient&#96;**  \\\\n  - Private constructor; use &#96;MiataruAndroidClient.Builder()&#96; then &#96;build()&#96;.\\\\n  - **Methods (all &#96;suspend&#96;):**\\\\n    - &#96;updateLocation(body: MiataruUpdateLocationRequest): Ack&#96;\\\\n    - &#96;getLocation(body: MiataruGetLocationRequest): MiataruGetLocationResponse&#96;\\\\n    - &#96;getLocationGeoJSON(deviceId: String): MiataruGetLocationGeoJSONResponse&#96;\\\\n    - &#96;getLocationHistory(body: MiataruGetLocationHistoryRequest): MiataruGetLocationHistoryResponse&#96;\\\\n    - &#96;getVisitorHistory(body: MiataruGetVisitorHistoryRequest): MiataruGetVisitorHistoryResponse&#96;\\\\n  - **&#96;MiataruAndroidClient.Builder&#96;:**  \\\\n    &#96;baseUrl&#96;, &#96;timeouts&#96;, &#96;enableLogging&#96;, &#96;addNetworkInterceptor&#96;, &#96;addApplicationInterceptor&#96;, &#96;build()&#96;.\\\\n\\\\n**Network (internal but defines API surface)**\\\\n\\\\n- **&#96;MiataruService&#96;** (Retrofit interface)  \\\\n  Same five operations as above, with &#96;@POST&#96;/&#96;@GET&#96; and JSON bodies/paths.\\\\n\\\\n**Models (all in &#96;com.miataru.client.model&#96;)**  \\\\n- **Core:** &#96;Ack&#96;, &#96;MiataruLocation&#96;  \\\\n- **UpdateLocation:** &#96;UpdateConfig&#96;, &#96;MiataruUpdateLocationRequest&#96; Summary of what was added to the plan:

**New section 2 – Android Studio: unified build, testing, and debugging**

- **2.1 Include the library**  
  In [src/settings.gradle.kts](src/settings.gradle.kts), add `include(":miataru-client")` and set `project(":miataru-client").projectDir = file("../Libraries/MiataruAndroidClient/miataru-client")` so the main project builds the app and the library. Open the **folder that contains `settings.gradle.kts`** (i.e. **src/**) in Android Studio as the project root.

- **2.2 Root build and version catalog**  
  In [src/build.gradle.kts](src/build.gradle.kts), add `alias(libs.plugins.android.library) apply false`. In [src/gradle/libs.versions.toml](src/gradle/libs.versions.toml), add the `android-library` plugin entry. In the library’s [build.gradle.kts](Libraries/MiataruAndroidClient/miataru-client/build.gradle.kts), use `alias(libs.plugins.android.library)` and `alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.android)` so the library uses the same AGP/Kotlin versions when built from the main project.

- **2.3 App dependency**  
  In [src/app/build.gradle.kts](src/app/build.gradle.kts), add `implementation(project(":miataru-client"))`.

- **2.4 Align SDK and JVM**  
  Align compileSdk, minSdk, targetSdk, and jvmTarget between app and library where it makes sense (e.g. one JDK 17 for the whole project).

- **2.5 Running and debugging**  
  Run/Debug the app with the default app run configuration. After adding tests (section 4), run library unit tests via Run Tests on `miataru-client` or the `:miataru-client:test` Gradle task. Run all tests from the Gradle tool window.

- **2.6 Run configurations**  
  Optionally add [src/.run](src/.run) with run configs for “Run app” and “Run miataru-client unit tests” and commit them so the team shares the same setups.

- **2.7 Porting plan**  
  In [documentation/AndroidPortingPlan.md](documentation/AndroidPortingPlan.md), state that the Android Studio project root is the folder containing `settings.gradle.kts` (the **src** directory) and add a short “Building, testing, and debugging with Android Studio” subsection that refers to the above.

- Old section 2 (library changes) is now **section 3**.  
- Old section 3 (tests) is now **section 4**, with a note that once the library is included (section 2), tests are run from Android Studio via `:miataru-client:test` or Run Tests.  
- Old sections 4 and 5 are now **5** and **6**.

**Summary (section 6)**

### How the plan ensures this

- **Unified Gradle project**:  
  Section **2** (“Android Studio: unified build, testing, and debugging”) explicitly makes `miataru-client` a **submodule** of the main Android Studio project (via `include(":miataru-client")` and `projectDir` in `src/settings.gradle.kts`).  
  → A single Gradle sync/build in Android Studio will compile **both**:
  - the **app** module (`:app`)
  - the **miataru-client** library module (`:miataru-client`)

- **Dependencies wired up**:  
  Section **2.3** adds `implementation(project(":miataru-client"))` to `app`, so the app builds **against the local client**.

- **IDE build / run / test**:  
  - Build: “Make Project” / Gradle `assemble` builds app + client.  
  - Run/Debug: standard **Run ‘app’** uses the library code.  
  - Tests: section **4** defines JVM tests for `miataru-client`; with the module included, Android Studio can run `:miataru-client:test` and app tests in one project.

So the plan is already structured so that **both the Android app and the Android miataru-client are built, tested, and debugged together in Android Studio**.

Summary of what was implemented:

## 1. Porting plan document ([documentation/AndroidPortingPlan.md](documentation/AndroidPortingPlan.md))
- **Project root**: Documented that the Android Studio project root is the folder that contains `settings.gradle.kts` (`src/`).
- **Miataru client – API 1.1**: New section with link to Miataru.yaml, relationship to the iOS client, and API 1.1 breaking/additive changes (RequestMiataruDeviceID/Key, DeviceKey, new endpoints, GetLocationGeoJSON 401).
- **Building, testing, and debugging with Android Studio**: Subsection describing unified build, Run/Debug app, running library unit tests, and running all tests.
- **Checklists**: “Miataru client library – API 1.1” and “Miataru client library – tests” added at the top of the Implementation Checklist; “Miataru API client” clarified as app use of the miataru-client library.

## 2. Android Studio unified build
- **[src/settings.gradle.kts](src/settings.gradle.kts)**: `include(":miataru-client")` and `project(":miataru-client").projectDir = file("../Libraries/MiataruAndroidClient/miataru-client")`.
- **[src/build.gradle.kts](src/build.gradle.kts)**: `alias(libs.plugins.android.library) apply false`.
- **[src/gradle/libs.versions.toml](src/gradle/libs.versions.toml)**: `android-library` plugin entry.
- **[src/app/build.gradle.kts](src/app/build.gradle.kts)**: `implementation(project(":miataru-client"))`.
- **[Libraries/MiataruAndroidClient/miataru-client/build.gradle.kts](Libraries/MiataruAndroidClient/miataru-client/build.gradle.kts)**: Plugins switched to `alias(libs.plugins.android.library)` and `alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.android)` so the library uses the root version catalog when built from `src/`.

## 3. Miataru client library – models and API
- **Models.kt**:  
  - `MiataruLocation`: optional `deviceKey`, `speed`, `batteryLevel`, `altitude`.  
  - `RequestConfig`: optional `requestMiataruDeviceKey`.  
  - `MiataruGetLocationDevice`: optional `deviceKey`.  
  - `GetVisitorHistoryPayload`: optional `deviceKey`.  
  - `GeoJsonProperties`: optional `timestamp`, `horizontalAccuracy`, `speed`, `batteryLevel`, `altitude`.  
  - New types: DeleteLocation, SetDeviceKey, SetAllowedDeviceList, SetDeviceSlogan, GetDeviceSlogan request/response payloads and `ErrorResponse`.
- **MiataruService.kt**: New endpoints – `getLocationGeoJSONPost`, `deleteLocation`, `setDeviceKey`, `setAllowedDeviceList`, `setDeviceSlogan`, `getDeviceSlogan`.
- **MiataruAndroidClient.kt**: New suspend functions for the above; `getLocationGeoJSON(body)` overload; `API_VERSION = "1.1.0"`.
- **README.md**: Updated for API 1.1, YAML reference, and 401/403 behavior and new endpoints.

## 4. Tests
- **miataru-client/build.gradle.kts**: Added `testImplementation` for JUnit 4, kotlinx-coroutines-test, Moshi, and MockWebServer.
- **[ModelsTest.kt](Libraries/MiataruAndroidClient/miataru-client/src/test/kotlin/com/miataru/client/model/ModelsTest.kt)**: Moshi round-trip tests for MiataruLocation, RequestConfig, GetVisitorHistoryPayload, Ack, DeleteLocation, SetDeviceKey, MiataruAllowedDevice, GetDeviceSlogan response, ErrorResponse, and DeleteLocationResponse.
- **[MiataruAndroidClientTest.kt](Libraries/MiataruAndroidClient/miataru-client/src/test/kotlin/com/miataru/client/MiataruAndroidClientTest.kt)**: MockWebServer tests for builder base URL, updateLocation, getLocation, getLocationHistory, getVisitorHistory, deleteLocation, setDeviceKey, and `API_VERSION`.

## 5. Run configurations
- **[src/.run/Run app.run.xml](src/.run/Run app.run.xml)** and **[src/.run/Run miataru-client unit tests.run.xml](src/.run/Run miataru-client unit tests.run.xml)** added so the app and miataru-client unit tests can be run from the IDE.

**Note**: Unit tests were not run in this environment because `JAVA_HOME` was not set. In Android Studio, open the **src** folder as the project root, sync Gradle, then run **Run > Run miataru-client unit tests** or the Gradle task `:miataru-client:test` to execute the tests.
